- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to underpredict prices; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.3), model overpredicts; reduce forecast by 1–3% to align with true mean reversion.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive — apply lag correction: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day post-spike.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, forecast should not drop below 1–2% below recent low; if rising, avoid exceeding 2–3% above recent high.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates late-period price surges (especially after sentiment shifts to positive); add 0.5–1.5% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment >0.5.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.2–0.8), model tends to overfit short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values before final prediction.
